messages.subject: Embedding Stan in C++ application
parts:

I wanted to know whether it is possible to incorporate Stan in another C++ application. Since it is also written in C++, there should be a way. Currently, I am using RInside to call rstan but then you have all this data transferring which is time-consuming.

Thanks in advance for your help

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Embedding Stan in C++ application
parts:
What specifically did you want from Stan? We're about
to separate out the math library into a standalone include --- that
contains all the matrix, probability, and autodiff code.
All of the MCMC and transform and I/O code is callable through
C++, as is the translator from a Stan program to a C++ class.

- Bob

On Sunday, July 12, 2015 at 8:10:26 AM UTC-4, Ulf Mertens wrote:
I wanted to know whether it is possible to incorporate Stan in another C++ application. Since it is also written in C++, there should be a way. Currently, I am using RInside to call rstan but then you have all this data transferring which is time-consuming.

At the moment, this is not as easy as it should be. If you were going to invest (a lot of) effort on this, I think it would be best spent helping us with (the closed but not merged pull request)

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/1210

If essentially all Stan functions that currently take an Eigen::Matrix<> (including vectors) were to be generalized so that they could also take an Eigen::Map<>, then (after some more changes), an external application could pass Stan a pointer to its data objects (and the relevant dimensions).

Ben

parts:
Daniel's rewriting the services layer so that it will be
like calling CmdStan only from within C++.

All the I/O is handled through callbacks. var_context
on the reading side, and various write wrappers on the output
side. That is, there's no serialization format or files
indicated at the C++ API level.

Stanc generates the Stan model class, which has a constructor
which loads data into memory through a var_context. This instantiated
model class is what's used as an argument to all the algorithms.

You can implement the writers to stream the output data wherever
you want. It gets called one draw at a time. CmdStan streams to
a file.

Let us know if you have more specific questions.

- Bob

Hi John,

CmdStan has examples of how you can access the underlying Stan C++ from a C++ executable. We don't have this doc'ed because there hasn't been any real demand for it.

Ulf, to see how this is done, see stan-dev/cmdstan's src/cmdstan directory. See command.hpp (main.hpp just includes and calls command.hpp; this is going to be much simpler in the future). I don't have the time to deal with it now, but please remind me in about a month.


Daniel

On Friday, June 10, 2016 at 3:26:00 PM UTC-4, John Hall wrote:
I'm not sure what the best practice is here. Is it possible to pipe the data? I see some questions from SO on calling exes from within C++ programs, has anyone tried this?

I don't know of anyone who has tried hard to get this to work, in part because it would be hard. But it is perhaps easier than it was a couple of weeks ago using the DLL sublibrary in Boost 1.61.0

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_61_0/doc/html/boost_dll.html

I speculate that if you compiled your Stan program without a main() function (like how rstan and pystan does it) into a shared object that you could import that using Boost DLL. But it would still be a challenge to do the I/O. In particular, unless you want a CSV file of output, you would have to do something to store the draws in memory. Maybe some of the new writers stuff would help with this.

If I were doing this, I would call R from C++ using the RInside package.

Ben

On Sunday, June 12, 2016 at 12:11:49 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:

Hi John,

CmdStan has examples of how you can access the underlying Stan C++ from a C++ executable. We don't have this doc'ed because there hasn't been any real demand for it.

Ulf, to see how this is done, see stan-dev/cmdstan's src/cmdstan directory. See command.hpp (main.hpp just includes and calls command.hpp; this is going to be much simpler in the future). That's how to call Stan from C++. You obviously don't need all of it. If you just wanted to run NUTS from the command line with known file locations, it should be a 20 line executable (+ includes). I don't have the time to deal with it now, but please remind me in about a month.


Daniel
